tips.comment: I really rate Rosallion and he ran a blinder at Royal Ascot but it is hard to look past the brilliant Field Of Gold. Since finishing an unlucky 2nd in the 2000 Guineas he has looked imperious since and should be difficult to beat.
Has been slowly coming to hand this year, and the latest run at Ascot was another good effort. Reported to be in great form and huge value here against the favorite.

Multiple Group-winning runner who scored in last year's Breeder's Cup in a Group 1 mile race. Well beaten by Field of Gold at Ascot last time out but was equally well clear of 3rd place. 3-year-olds getting the weight allowance is a big positive, and it might come down to a tussle with the Gosden runner again. Goodwood is a different test than Ascot, and at the prices, it's worth a chance on the well-drawn Henri Matisse laying down a stiffer challenge this time out.

I did think a chance could be taken on the Aussie runner Carl Spackler here. His jockey took a firm grip on him off a slow early pace at Ascot, and he just got done for a turn of foot late on. The time backs up the fact it was a slowly run affair, and, considering his keenness, he stuck to the task well enough, and off a likely strong pace round a bend here he could be seen to much better effect. I feel like he could be one of the first to get to the pacemakers, and if he’s filled up enough he could prove harder to peg back falling down the hill. He has the class to be involved in this from his runs in the US, and overall I just thought he was far too big a price even if giving 8 lbs to some sparkling 3-year-olds is a tough ask.

Docklands was an Ascot Group One winner and narrowly beat Rosallion with a late burst. Consistent and thrives in the distance. May lack the class of Field of Gold but offers a strong place if the pace suits.

He has a pretty consistent profile up to this trip and went down in a photo finish at Ascot two months ago on his first start for 6 months before a disappointing run in the Royal Hunt Cup back there last time. He refused to settle then, but hopefully that won’t be the case here moving into Group 1 company. He is probably playing for minor honours given the quality of the opposition.

Lady Iman drops back in distance to five furlongs at which she started her career impressively. She lost her unbeaten record to Beautify last time over 6f in a Group 2 at the Curragh but can pick up a Group 3 prize here.

Charlie Appleby (SR 33%) trained, Godolphin colt Military Code hasn't done a lot wrong in four starts so far. Disappointed in the Coventry Stakes (failed to give his true running there) but back to form when beaten a neck in the Listed Dragon Stakes at Sandown over five furlongs last time. Maybe a little unlucky there (the pace a little too strong) and still finished two lengths clear of the remainder. Goodwood five furlongs looks to suit. Can be played at odds of 7-2.
Worth an each-way bet as he was a close 2nd in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes at Royal Ascot and is worth backing each-way here.

Sands of Spain has maintained a progressive profile over 5f, following two wins at Carlisle and Newcastle before finishing a sound third in the Super Sprint at Newbury. An effort that came under handicap conditions when conceding weight to the front two, yet still showing promise despite losing focus on the front end. Rated 91 and currently given a generous price at writing, he holds potential to outrun that price if he secures a clean trip in this competitive Group 3 since several rivals, including Lady Iman and Military Code, may face traffic or tactical challenges. With the race likely to involve a fierce early pace, Sands of Spain's battling style and upward trajectory give him solid claims to get in the frame.

The odds to bet on Rydale Frosty seem to be really generous, considering that it has improved with every race. It finished 4th in its first one here in Goodwood at the beginning of June, then 2nd in Newmarket, and finally winning a few days ago in Windsor. Its shape could give Rydale Frosty another win.

Very consistent filly who put up a fine effort in a Grp2 Lto over 6f @ Newmarket, coming 3/6 beaten 3.75 lengths. Drops down to Grp3 company here, has plenty of pace so this 5f will suit and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 14/1 very good Ew value here.
Ameeq is an improver who I think would have done better than 4th on GF in his first G2 last month if he had not been hit on the nose by a rival's whip. I expect more today.

He's already a dual winner from four starts. After winning in Wetherby, he struggled in deep waters at Ascot and Sandown. He has a booking of a notable jockey and is from a good stable and should impress.
Zelaina led the field in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot before fading into 8th place. She should appreciate the fast 5f course at Goodwood.
This filly is decent and now dropping slightly in class she can go very close today. Her yard are in good health too.

OUR KODY has won a race at 5f. A winner on her latest outing over 5f at Windsor last month, winning easily. Course, distance, and going should suit and could well be able to go in again and win this race.

Only just touched off in a decent maiden @ Listowel on debut and then only beaten 5.75 lengths in a Grp2 over 6f @ Curragh on follow up run. Drops down to a class 2 here, showed plenty of pace on debut so this 5f is fine, top jockey booked and very good Irish trainer is 1/3 with his 2yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 the Ew value against hot favourite.

Zelaina takes up a fair chunk of the market here, and perhaps rightly. However, it does make the others perhaps bigger than they should be on balance, and I thought Lebron Power could have a say. She was last off the bridle in the Dragon Stakes, but only because she got stuck in behind the leaders as Staya and Military Code circled the field with clear runs. Had she got an out at the right time, she’d have finished much closer to the pair as by the time she got clear air, her race was run. She’ll evidently want further in time on breeding, but if she can get out as sharply as she did on debut, hopefully she can make the most of that extra stamina in a race that simply won’t lack for pace. Her dam appreciated some dig in the ground, so she shouldn’t mind the seemingly softer surface.

Angel Numbers ran some good sectionals on her debut in Chepstow, beating Our Cody in the process. She didn't find much on the uphill finish in Beverly next, but she was given some more time to mature and can run a good race today. E/W money. GL.
Has raced more than any other in the field and that includes a victory over this distance at Lingfield Park in May. Has good pace and over 5f could surprise.

Promise to take from her four starts, the best being her debut run at Salisbury when 3rd. The latest effort saw her run a close 3rd at Lingfield over 5f, and her chances of improving on that probably depend on how she reacts to first-time cheekpieces and a tongue tie. Could reward each-way support at massive odds if the experiment works.

I was all over Sing Us A Song for the King George Handicap at Ascot but he came out of the stalls very slowly and raced plum last for most of the way. He made up a lot of ground late on to eventually finish 9th not beaten that far. The price here is disappointing but I have got to give him one more chance as he previously looked very progressive.

Sudu was impressive when he was let go at Epsom last time, and there looked to be plenty more to come off the back of that effort. Barely given a tap, he extended to be a 7L winner in the last furlong and gets hit with a 13lb rise. He’s 2lbs well in on that rating hike though, and looked like he could be going places with that effort so is taken to follow up here. Varian isn’t having the best of times, but has won two of the last four runnings of this.

Looks certain to at least finish in the first 3. Ran well when 3rd over 10f at Newmarket last time off a mark of 89. Had previously won at Haydock over today's trip and the step back up in distance will suit. The rain arriving yesterday was an added bonus and should provide a welcome boost to trainer Alan King after the sad loss of Trueshan yesterday.

Novelista is still a maiden but has been beaten in photo finishes in his last two races over 14f. The drop in distance to 12f may not be ideal, but if the going goes softer, it will be to his advantage. He ran behind Sing Us A Song at Goodwood over 10f as a two-year-old when they were 1st and 3rd in a maiden off level weights. He now gets ten pounds with William Buick riding him for Charlie Johnson, who likes to get a few winners at Glorious Goodwood.
Comes out of an Ascot race that really has proved to be a decent enough yardstick since, with the 2nd place coming 2nd to Lambourn in the Irish Derby. Worth these odds.
9/1 for JUPITER AMMON makes plenty of appeal. New Bay brings a 25% SR (A/E 1.33) with colts and this unexposed som of his could improve ten fold.

Is in good form. Easily won last time out over 12 furlongs. Dropping back in trip but up in grade. His best results have come when getting to the front early and I would expect him to make an early move in that respect. Yard are in good form, they go well here too. Well bred and notable jockey booking.

Considering his pedigree, this purchase was quite inexpensive, and he continues to show improvement. He struggled at Southwell but just fell short on his handicap debut at Haydock after being off for 6 months. He demonstrated resilience when he rectified his performance with a more assertive strategy at Doncaster 11 days ago and should have more potential. The current odds of 18/1 are fantastic for an each-way bet.
Showed quality earlier in the year with wins on the all weather at Southwell, Newcastle and Kempton Park. Struggled since but has gained good experience over this distance and could surprise a few.

Tabiti won a fillies G3 back in September. Although only third in a handicap on the return from the break in a C2 last month, she will be all the better for that run. I would expect improvement while carrying 8-13 today in this G3.

Finished first in this race last year but placed second after drifting off her racing line and interfering with Raqiya. Back as a 4-year-old, having run well in Listed and Group company without winning anything significant. A couple of all-weather runs have been disappointing, though she was drawn very wide last time out at Chelmsford.
Bright Thunder is probably good value for these odds here, having run well in a Listed Race last time at Deauville. Can build on this to win.

3-year-olds have won the last three runnings of the Oak Tree, and that's the age group I'm concentrating on. Andrew Balding's Formal was highly impressive at Epsom on Oaks day, but then proceeded to disappoint at York against the boys in the G3 Criterion. She was the only 3-year-old to contest that race, and I'm happy to put a line through that run.

Romantic Style is the 2nd of William's 5 rides today. The Charlie Appleby-trained for the Boys in Blue, Romantic Style is 2nd top-rated in this Grp3 on a mark of 106. She has 4 wins from 9 starts and has won in this grade and on this ground. The 4yo Night of Thunder filly should have every chance in this race against her own sex.

Arabian Dusk is a 3-year-old filly trained by Simon and Ed Crisford and ridden by Harry Davies. She is in stall 8, which is not ideal for a prominent runner but manageable with cover here. She has had 9 runs with 1 win and 4 places, giving her an 11% win rate and 56% place rate. She ran respectably in Group 3 company last time out over 6f, finishing fourth by 2 lengths at York. That followed a strong second in the Sandy Lane, a race that has franked her form. She handles good ground and 6f is her best trip, so 7f may be a good spot here as she holds on well. Back in calmer waters here also and with her class form, she is at least a solid each-way chance if settling early. Pace should be honest today.

Tabiti looks fairly solid overall, but is short enough and has to step up here on what she’s done so far. The 3yo’s hold sway in here on adjusted ratings, but perhaps Cloud Cover could prove a bit of a fly in the ointment at the top of them. She travelled so well into the race last time when looking to have plenty under the bonnet, extending clear in the last furlong. If she can transfer that form onto the turf she could be worth her rating and is the only older horse that sticks out in that regard. She’s entitled to come on for her first run since April, and she stays further than this, so assuming she can transfer to turf having had just 2 runs on it from 19 starts overall I think she’s worth her chance in this higher grade. Stall 1 is a concern if she gets caught too far back, but the race has been won from low draws so I’m happy to overlook that.

This could blow this field away or come stone last, hence the win tip. Returned this year with a decent 2nd at Epsom and went one better with a listed win at Carlisle. The going is the unknown having only raced on softer ground, but if not withdrawn and the good ground isn't a problem, could win this wide open race.

CD winner who was on a hat-trick last time out after winning two previous runs but was an unlucky 9th of 25 at Royal Ascot after not getting a clear run. Runs off the same 95 rating today after a refreshing 40-day break.
Excuses last time when pulled up at Royal Ascot. Her form reads well otherwise and has strong form over this course. The drop in trip will suit, and despite a wide draw, she rates a strong player.

I'm glad i got on this yesterday because the price has dropped a lot. Has been improving for a little while now and this 5yo still appears to be learning and getting better. Up in grade so won't be easy, but this looks like a race in which many have good chances, so still at a reasonable price looks the value ew pick.

Fair Angelica looks a little underrated here. Yes, there is still the possibility of some improvement from one or two rivals, but on turf, over the trip, we could say the same about the selection. If there is any ease in the ground at all after predicted overnight showers, she may be a fly in the ointment.
Given a freshen up after a solid run at Longchamp last time and has a really good previous record when fresh, so should run well at big odds.

Race 5 at Goodwood today is the British Stallion Handicap for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,990 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old filly Music Piece from the Andrew Balding yard, and will be ridden by Oisin Murphy. This daughter of Camelot is back to her best distance on what she has shown so far, with her 2nd over this course and distance two starts back a good enough pointer. She must have a decent chance on form and should be included.

Wonder Star is an unexposed filly with only three runs. She won a maiden at Ascot in good style and then was tried in a listed race only 8 days later at Newbury, where she was only 8th of 10 but received a bump over a furlong out and weakened. Her mark of 82 gives her a good chance in this field.

Even though a 7-year-old, his form of beating Westridge at Windsor two runs ago (who won yesterday in good style) suggests a 5lb rise may not be enough to stop him. He flopped last time, but a lot went wrong at Southwell on the all-weather there, while he is also 0/10 on the all-weather and approximately 6lb worse according to RPRs. Now, stall 5 for a hold-up horse at Goodwood is a concern, but it is not the strongest of races, and I am prepared to chance it.
Very low weight, ran a big win last time out. Draw isn't too bad and will be up with the pace. 23% rider and jockey, should put up a bold bid.

Ashariba has some very consistent form figures apart from, arguably, a blip at Epsom in June. She will definitely get this trip, and if she's at the top of her game, she has a big chance. She will also act on good/good-soft ground if there's been rain.

A winner on her debut at Wolverhampton, she’s posted a couple of decent efforts on turf and was a close 5th in a listed event at Goodwood two starts ago. Back on the AW at Southwell for her handicap debut, going up in trip and ran well to finish 3rd. Decent claims here despite dropping back in trip.

Runner-up in this race last year when trained by Sir Michael Stoute, ironically beaten by a Ralph Beckett horse whose yard she joined in November 2024. Won on stable debut over a furlong further but most disappointed since most recently at Chester where the track and soft ground would not have suited. Ralph Beckett has won this race 3 times in the last 5 years so it is reasonable to assume Power Of Destiny has been targeted for this race and she looks a decent each way bet again this year.

This has been drifting in the market and is now best price of 20-1. Ok, is up in grade today and first two runs this year didn't look great, but was much better lto with a running on 2nd at Newmarket. But it's the new trip today that excites me and looks like this will help her no end. Also has a tongue tie added to the cheek pieces which could also improve her chances today. Ew for betting.
Patagonia Girl is a dual distance winner with solid form on similar ground. Excuses last time, and with a clearer run and light weight, she could surprise in a competitive field.

Has mixed form this season but does have a win and two seconds. Excuses at Southwell last time when racing wide and below par. Best efforts have been over 10f on a sound surface that she will get here. Place claims despite some inconsistency.
Got going late at Chester last time, and in a race that looks pretty thin outside the top couple, he will be able to get into the race earlier and run a reasonable race at odds.
Won well over 7f at Beverley and Wolverhampton at the back end of last season. Regression since but early signs in the market have been promising and this race looks wide open.
Looks a likely winner here as the race will be run to suit. Needing a strongly run 7f is perfect for him, and I expect him to pick off the front runner late on to win.

Unexposed 3yo, 2 wins from 6. Back on his game four weeks ago after a couple of below par return runs. He was a very close runner-up that day in a decent contest, the field strung out behind the front three, earning a high rating. Every chance of some more improvement. He now takes on older runners for the first time and receives a nice 7lb age allowance from 18 of the 19 rivals.

Won a good 7-furlong handicap race in this grade at Newmarket last time out. The O'Meara yard is in good form and generally does well in handicaps at Goodwood. Well drawn and interesting jockey booking for the yard too.
Following the same path as last year, running at Ascot and turned out four days later to finish 2nd in this race. 2lb lower this time around and should be in the mix again.

Physique is consistent, proven at the distance, and narrowly beaten last time when well-backed. Returns to peak form with Oisin Murphy aboard; strong course placer, primed to strike despite wide draw.

Another 3-year-old colt with an e/w chance is Beckett's runner, who finished down the field in the Britannia Stakes LTO. But this class 3 is far easier. The trainer has a decent w/p strike rate at the track, and the colt remains unbeaten in all his races at this level and below, as well as a 2 y/o win at this festival last year over C+D.
Crimson Spirit comes into today after three C4 wins, with the latest win being by a bigger margin after taking on more weight. This makes me think this C3 could be within his grasp. EW 5P.

RACINGBREAKS RYDER enjoys it here, having placed in this last year and finishing second the last twice. He still looks pretty well handicapped and avoids the high draw so looks to have each-way claims if keeping to the recent form. Went off fav for the Racing League last week at Yarmouth and could get involved again.

Won this race last year off a pound lower mark. Not seen since stopping quickly when well supported but 11th of 12 over a mile on the Lingfield Polytrack. Comes here fresh following a break but will be ready to defend his crown.
The Cox Yard is in form, and there has been support for this last-time-out winner this morning. A three-pound rise for his win last time shouldn't be a stopper.

Great Acclaim is tried in a first-time hood. He had four wins last season, and his handicap mark went from 68 up to 92. Although not winning so far this year, he was only beaten a short head by Cracking Gold at Newmarket in his penultimate race off 88.

This C/D winners course record alone which stands @ 38 percent on this unique track would make them a good bet here. However, they also won this race in 2023, ran a great race in a class 2 handicap @ Haydock Lto after getting very badly hampered in the race, interesting change of jockey for this stable and excellent trainer is in form, making current 16/1 solid Ew value here.
Has made the frame on all five starts this year and is well worth a go at the prices to do the same today. Elizabeth Gale claims 5lbs.

Julie Camacho has always been very adept at lining her horses up on attractive handicap marks, and she's taken that to another level this season with several higher-grade handicappers landing some good prizes for her. Hopefully, this is another one to add to that roll call. Havana Blue's debut this season after a wind operation was full of promise, where she finished close up to Two Tribes, which has franked that form since. A look at previous winners of this race also shows that the winner is nearly always from a stable that lays one out (O'Meara, Evans, Fahey, etc.).

Has been progressing well but slightly disappointing on the last two runs. However, form boosted on the last run with Mister Bluebird winning a Racing League on Thursday. Unexposed now upped to 7f - has form on soft at 6f, so should have the stamina to cope with the extra furlong.

Didn't offer anything near to expectations at Newcastle last time out but suggestion is return to the turf will be a good fit. Has three victories on turf in France including last summer at Strasbourg.

Officially this is a drop in grade from Class 2 to Class 3 for outsider Mcmanaman who starts out for a new yard. First start this season also. Taylor Fisher claims a 3lbs allowance. Twice a winner at Meydan over seven furlongs for Doug Watson. Ran a couple of good races for Ian Williams last season. Looks up against it here in terms of class but has shown ability in the past.

This R M Beckett-trained 3-year-old filly can make it third time lucky today after finishing second in her first two races. The latest was over seven and a half furlongs on good ground at Chester when beaten 2 1/4 lengths behind the A M Balding-trained Mister Winston. So, with Edward Greatrex doing the steering, it looks like a win today.

Is becoming a habitual slow starter which is not a help, however if they can get a fast run race today and re-produce their effort 3 runs ago, then could be in the shake up here off current mark of 68. Good jockey/trainer combination makes current 25/1 worth Ew consideration against the very hot favourite.
Third in a better race last time and is down significantly in class and grade here. Lightly raced, having only had a single run at 2 years old. Has a decent chance of winning this.

Won her first race over 7 furlongs at Chester last time out, keeping on well inside the final half a furlong to suggest this first attempt at a mile will suit. She makes her handicap debut and could be on a good initial mark to take advantage.

Radiant Beauty is a 4-year-old filly trained by James Owen and ridden by Jason Hart. She is in stall number 1, which is ideal if breaking alertly. She has had 14 runs in total with 3 wins and 1 place, giving her a win rate of 21% and a place rate of 29%. She won two starts ago over this distance off a mark of 75 and now runs off 77, which looks okay still based on her latest defeat. All three wins have come on the AW, and she is yet to fully convince me on turf, although she has gone close, so giving her a shot here. With her handy draw and prominent running style, she has a good chance if reproducing her AW form. The pace should be fair also.

Only 2-36 and hasn't really threatened to add a 3rd victory so far this season, but has slipped to a career-low mark. Both wins did come at this time of year, so while he's certainly not one for maximum faith, he is worth a speculative investment this afternoon.
Maiden ran poorly last time when plum last in Ayr handicap. Hopefully, will get better ground here and has course and distance form previously.
A beaten favourite off this mark of 55 over course and distance when sent off favourite in April 2025. Denied a clear run in that race, beaten a length and may have won with a clearer passage.
Crocus Time moved stables recently and on last effort produced a really good run to finish 3rd over this trip at Thirsk. Has a good draw here and with a lot of these not firing, she has every chance.

Ran on very well Lto after getting outpaced, coming 5/11 beaten 3.5 lengths in a similar class handicap over 5f @ Beverley. Down 2lb here, step up to this 6f a plus, good jockey up and very shrewd trainer who is in top form @ present, is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 21 percent with a Lsp of 46.25, making current 14/1 solid Ew value in the race.
No comment made
Sandret returns to a winning course, drops in trip, and has strong class form. Likely fitter now, and with a low weight, could spring a surprise if rediscovering past turf form.

This jockey has been on board the last three times the horse has won. Stepping up to seven furlongs looks like a plus. Third run back after a break, and looking back at the form, the horse has a history of hitting form out of the blue. Dropped two pounds and not far off the last winning weight.
Forest Caper's siblings suggest that this horse will be well suited by this increase in trip here and is a well deserved favourite.
Sir Mark Prescott stepping horse up in trip should relish the step up. Trainer in good form, and Poppy rides well for trainer. Big player.

Race 3 at Redcar today is a Handicap (Class 5) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 2,012 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding King Chaos from the Rebecca Menzies yard, and will be ridden by Charlie Bennett. This son of Woodman is a fair sort and returns to his optimum distance here. Along with some fair form, he rates a main danger in this field.

Triple Force won two C6 back in June at 1m2f. I think he would have done better in the third when trying 1m4f had the rider not dropped his whip. He goes again off the same mark for this C5 back at 1m2f and could be involved again EW.

The yard has a really good record in this race, having won 3 out of the last 5 renewals with 3-year-olds. Below par last time at York over 1m, but I'm hoping that a combination of the extra distance and a strong trainer strike rate at Redcar means Off Spin can run well.

I very much doubt that this horse will go off as big as 40/1 after the trainer landed a massive priced 4-timer from 5 runners yesterday. Clearly, her horses are running out of their skins at the moment. This horse's 4th of 8 in a novice race last summer for his previous trainer is good enough to go close here if you look at the horses around him in that race. The 2 runs this season have been to improve fitness, I suspect, and it could be all systems go now.
7th on debut in Ffos Las novice over the minimum trip when very slowly away. Should improve on that run here.
Decent pedigree and makes seasonal reappearance after running just once as a 2yo. Money has come for him, so it would appear he is fit to do himself justice.
This selection is a 2-year-old first time racing in today's contest. It has a good pedigree. Callum Rodriguez is first to be in the saddle. Hopeful it can go close. Hopeful of a good first run.

Naawi makes only his second start after a debut over 6f at Doncaster where he was slowly away, but stayed on strongly in the final furlong to finish 7th, passing several impressive rivals in the closing stages. Dropping slightly in trip and stepping into a small Class 4 novice field should suit his running style and aid a clean start. If Naawi gets a decent break and an untroubled trip, he could be a surprise today.

This W J Haggas-trained 3-year-old gelding won over one mile three furlongs on good ground at Hamilton and followed that up by running on well from the rear to only be beaten 1 3/4 lengths in third of the ten runners behind the C Johnston-trained Pole Star. So with Cieren Fallon onboard, he looks hard to oppose.

Won over half a furlong further at Chester on penultimate start and runner-up when a beaten favourite when dropped back in trip to a mile and a half at Ffos Las. This step back up in trip will suit and Sir Mark Prescott's yard are in top form with 5 winners from his last 24 runners, a 21% strike rate.

Has been placed in the last 2 runs in 3 career starts at Haydock over 12f and then 40 days ago at Goodwood over today's 14f trip. Has an opening handicap mark of 78 and is open to further progression.
Won over this distance at Ffos Las last time out and was unlucky over CD the time before when denied a clear run to finish a close 4th. The 10/1 in this 6-horse race is a crazy price.

Scarlet Moon, trained by Archie Watson and ridden by Hollie Doyle, has found his feet this spring with three all-weather wins before tackling turf. The gelding remains lightly raced on grass and ran below par in his latest 14f at Ffos Las when hampered at the start and was unable to get his usual stalking rhythm. Prior to that setback, he scored over 12f at both Southwell and Kempton this season, demonstrating strong cruising speed and grit to dominate his rivals in style. Dropping to 1m 6f, the conditions appear ideal for him to get back to winning form, especially if he can lead or be prominent early.

This expensive C Appleby-trained colt made a promising racecourse debut over seven furlongs on good ground at Haydock 27 days ago when only beaten one length in second behind the G Boughey-trained Protection Act. With improvement expected, he can go one place better today with D C Costello taking over in the saddle.
Given a gentle introduction to racing on debut when finishing 5th, will be much more on the ball for that run, and the jockey's handy 5lbs claim could play a part here.

Shaped promisingly on his racecourse debut over an extended 7f at Haydock at the end of May and did well to finish a close 4th without getting a hard ride. Slightly down in trip for his second start at York but showed some improvement and should be involved here.
Showed some decent form before being well beaten in the Norfolk Stakes at Royal Ascot. Drops to a more suitable grade here and should go close.

The stable is in tremendous form at the moment with a brilliant strike rate over the last 14 days. Won last time out over this trip, Hollie Doyle on board again, and a follow-up is very much possible.

Race 2 at Sandown today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 2-year-olds over 1,014 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2yo filly Country Artiste from the Clive Cox yard, and will be ridden by Hector Crouch. This son of Supremacy is down in class here after a good performance last time out and should be a major player in this field.
Is Evidently a Winner in waiting judged on recent efforts, and Earthwatch must have a stellar chance here you would think.
Found out in a much better race last time and drops significantly in grade here. Down into a 0-70 for the first time on turf.

Just the one selection for tomorrow, and on my current form, it's probably for good reason lol. This horse can run much better than the last time out effort when only 9th of 10 at Newbury this month. But now, just 3 lbs higher than the last winning mark, and with some improvements, I do fancy his chances.

Great Blasket didn't do badly last year but changed yards and has not been great since the break in April. However, he did grab a win at Chepstow last month on good ground but could not follow up on GF last time out. Today's mark is still 4 lbs below last year's C3 good winning mark and worth another shot in this C4.

Caledonian, trained by David Simcock and partnered with 5lb claimer Tayn Langley, is a lightly raced 3-year-old who could be set to bounce back now dropped to a mile in a small field apprentice handicap. After shaping with promise as a two-year-old, including a convincing win at Kempton, he has faltered in progress. The drop in trip looks like a deliberate move, and he now faces weaker opposition today. With the apprentice allowance helping his weight burden and the return to a mile possibly unlocking improvement, Caledonian looks like a worthwhile bet at this price.

Race 1 at Sandown today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,609 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 9-year-old gelding Tempus from the Archie Watson yard, and will be ridden by Laura Goughlin. This son of Kingman is well handicapped in this race and can easily land his 11th win of his career in this small field of six.

With the early runs being steady enough and lokos capable of now applying that form in handicaps and looks a fair opening mark so expected to go well and as this is the only runner at the course for the trainer and jockey I'll take it

Will come on for the run last time, which was her first for 11 months. Finished 3rd in that run, not having run on the most advantageous part of the track. Blinkers added for the first time and comes here from the same mark.

Kimeko Glory has not done badly since the return with a 1414, with the latest fourth being in a C4. He has now changed yards and dropped to C5 off the same mark, all of which makes him worth an EW for me.

A beaten favourite over a mile here on penultimate start, 2nd of 6 beat a length and a half. Last of 6 in a Class 3 over a mile at Ascot last time out but the ease in grade to Class 5 will be easier. Steps up in trip but is out of Derby winner Sea The Stars and this 3 year old is likely to progress over further.
Consistent filly and is down in grade here, back into a 0-75/Class 5 for the first time since being placed off this mark 3 runs back. Decent each-way chance.

Won comfortably over CD last September, but hasn't done much since. The trainer's horses are in really good form at the moment with 3 winners from their last 5 runners. Got to be worth a go at 14/1, being the only CD winner in the field.
Distance suits and has been running over shorter distances more often than not. Was blocked twice on its previous run in the last furlong, hindering the win.
Extremely difficult to oppose. Twice second from two runs. The second of her races was at Royal Ascot where she was runner up in a class 1 where she was a 66/1 shot.

Late-foaled, Stolen was sent off 11/10 favourite in a $26k claiming race at Woodbine in May (5 furlongs on dirt) and duly obliged. She remains in the ownership of Norman Court Stud, and the filly is in the hands of a trainer who is in hot form at the moment. At the price (15/2), Stolen has to be underestimated.
No comment made
Showed promising form last autumn but got no run on return at Haydock. Might be the value pick with Aspull running under a penalty.

Miss Allsorts makes her belated debut. Unraced as a 2-year-old, she is a nicely bred filly who could be capable of winning races this season. If tuned up for her debut run, she could outrun her huge odds.
Carson is aboard this horse once again. 2 wins from 2 and looking for the hat-trick here tonight. Last run 6 days ago, and winning by 3l. Well backed for this run.
From a decent family who has done okay in maiden and novice company. Has shown greenness and should appreciate the extra distance. My NAP bet.
No comment made

Glint Of Light is a 3-year-old filly trained by Hughie Morrison and ridden by Lewis Edmunds. She has had 3 runs, no wins, 1 place so far, giving her an approximate 33% place rate. Hampered last time out, and now she is in stall number 1, which could be ideal for her handy early position. She makes her handicap debut off a mark of 62, which looks very workable. She has run respectably over similar trips and now drops slightly in trip with conditions looking to be in her favor. The race should be run at a good pace, and I expect her to be positioned prominently and hopefully capitalize here.
Been running consistently and has shown his ability with an excellent run last time. Must have a strong chance with stable in form.

The form on the all-weather is decent with two wins and two seconds. A reproduction of that kind of level on good ground would give him a chance in a poor race. Same mark as the second at Lingfield two runs back and seven pounds below the highest one. Only had four turf runs and some of those were in testing conditions, so scope to improve on this surface. Looks overpriced in a winnable race.
This horse came 1st of 5, 9 days ago, and no penalty for that race. Running off the same mark certainly makes her competitive here. Distance is no problem.

Looks more to come from this horse. Trainer sticks a 7lb claimer jockey in the saddle for his first-time ride. Had 2 runs at this track, with 1 win. The horse that finished 2nd, when this horse had its first win, has competed in class 1 & 2 events, finishing in respectable place positions. Suggest Dinamo has more to come in this class 6 event.

Tricky event here. This horse has had a spin around this track, finishing a respectable 4th. The horse that finished 2nd that day was a runner against today's favorite, 'Dinamo,' by 2 lengths. Suggest that at this mark, an each-way play is likely here.

Baybe Driver makes his handicap debut, having been gelded since the last run. He showed a little promise in the middle of his three runs to date and should improve for the switch to handicaps. He is related to plenty of winners, including a multiple sprint winner.
Looks to have a much better draw than last time and if she gets a clear run then she should be capable of challenging here for the spoils. Weighted well.

Hipop De Loire was beaten into 2nd place by a stablemate in a maiden hurdle here last year. That is his only hurdling experience to date, but he has had a recent run on the flat in a Listed race at Roscommon over 12f, where he was slightly hampered, running on late into 4th place. Looks the likely winner for Willie Mullins.
Won very well in National Hunt Flat. Debut over hurdles. Trainer in good form and should do well here against the favorite of Willie Mullins, who isn't in the best of form.

Kept on well Lto after getting outpaced on approach to the last, coming 2/21 beaten 1.25 lengths in a maiden hurdle over extended 2.3 miles @ Punchestown. Has a very large stamina dosage so the big step back up in distance going to suit, very good jockey back up and top trainer has done well here last 5 seasons, making current 8.50 very good Ew value in the race.

5th of 14 at Wexford earlier this month in a race that has since seen promise from some of those finishing in front. Question marks over short priced favourite Hipop De Loire and the 40/1 on Mighty Berkshire looks worth a poke.

Didn’t show a lot in his sole start in points but made a promising rules debut at Cork earlier this month when 4th of 18 in a three mile novice. Should be improvement to come and well worth considering.

This horse was a non-runner last time out when the money came for him. He steps up 2 furlongs today and is from a trainer and owner that know the time of day. He is worth a small E/W play in this race.
No comment made
Good first start over fences recently and has set him up perfectly for this. His class can hopefully overcome inexperience over fences and can go close.

2nd at the Cheltenham Festival in one of the Premier Handicap Chases and looking as if well ahead of his mark that day. Comes here just 2lb higher, giving him an excellent chance. Off for a couple of months but has run well after similar breaks previously.

This is very competitive, but Anyway still seems to be improving. He ran a cracker at the Cheltenham Festival behind subsequent Grade 1 winner Caldwell Potter and had a nice pipe opener recently when he comfortably beat the useful You Oughta Know. He has run well at the track before, gets this trip, and his prominent running style should keep him out of trouble. Derek O'Connor is in the saddle, which is also a positive.
Cian Collins has said it's been laid out for this. Ground has gone its way, little unsure about the distance but the ground and Cobden on board is enough for me to back it.
The 10 lb rise will not help things today, but like another i tipped earlier in the week, this is a horse on the rise imo. Trip will be fine and has ew chances at least.
Adamantly Chosen is the choice of Paul Townend here, and although he has not won since March 2023, his best run last season was probably his last in April when 3rd in a similar race at Punchestown.

He's entered to run in the Galway Plate. I'm hopeful he will skip that encounter to run in this race, a race he's done well in over the years.
Admittedly, he ran well below par in this event last season. To be fair, a mark of 150 probably stretched him. He was well beaten back in 8th place.
He runs off a 2 lbs lower mark this time around, with the jockey taking off 7 lbs. He had the assistance of a 5 lbs claiming jockey last term, so essentially he's running off a 4 lbs lower mark this season.
He's previously finished twice in this race, with the latest being back in 2023. He was beaten a head off a 2 lbs lower mark than this. He's obviously got the assistance of a 7 lbs claiming jockey this season, essentially making him 5 lbs lower than the mark he ran off in 2023.
He comes into this off the back of a win, so confidence is high. He looks a solid each-way bet to my eye.

Joseph O'Brien has some strong chances including the fav but I fancy Common Practice could claim this prize. He's run just 4 times over fences, winning twice including beating High Class Hero off level weights in a Grade 3 novice at Thurles - that rival rated 148 after finishing 3rd in the Sandown Gold Cup. Ran well at Punchestown after to finish 4th behind Sea Music (reopposes today) when carrying top weight and since shown his well-being with a 3rd on the flat at the Curragh. Has run well at Galway before and a mark of 141 looks to have potential; normal cheekpieces are replaced by blinkers today and with trip and ground ideal I'm expecting a big effort.
Finished 3rd beaten a length in this race last year, 4 lb higher this time around, but a very useful claimer on board taking off 7. Must be in with a shout.

Seems a decent pick for the win tip here because it's capable of winning if it gets to the finish, which it hasn't in the last 4 outings. Was 2nd here last year and i always think course form is a big benefit, so has outside chances at a big 33-1 price.

Recent victory in a chase at Kilbeggan in June. Finished a strong 2nd out of 9 in a handicap chase at Killarney just 22 days ago. Now stepping up in distance, he has the potential to make an impact here, and an each-way bet seems like a great deal at 66/1.

Sujet is in stall 5, which is fine for his running style and should help him settle early in midfield. Trained by Dermot Weld and ridden by Chris Hayes, he has had 4 runs, winning once and placing twice, giving him a 25% win rate and 75% place rate. He took a good step forward when winning a 3yo handicap at the Curragh last time off 77, winning extremely well and looking strong at the finish. That effort came on good ground, which suits him, and he looks well treated off 87 given his upward profile. The Frankel colt is progressive and should be suited by an honest pace, giving him a definite win chance, I reckon.

Far From Dandy went into many notebooks after his latest run, where he lost several lengths at the start by rearing as the stalls opened. He made up most of the ground by 2f out but found himself short of room and had to switch right, running on into 3rd place. He has been put back up to a mark of 80, and Jack Kearney, who rode him in his previous two races, takes over from Colin Keane. Should go close if starting well.

The model I run suggests Mathan can win this one. Mathan lines up here with the highest RPR of the 10-runner field. Official ranking leaves Mathan well treated in the weights and carries less than both the current favorite and top weight. Plenty of form in the figures and drawn in stall 9, but over 1m it shouldn't make a huge difference over the distance. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Refreshment arrives at Galway in top form and chasing a hat trick after back to back wins at Leopardstown and Cork. He first caught the eye when powering home from midfield to score over a mile at Leopardstown, showing an excellent turn of foot and strong finishing kick. He backed that up with a dominant front running display at Cork just five days later, defying a 6lb rise, suggesting there's more to come off his current mark. With a good racing weight and confidence high, he looks well placed to challenge this evening.

Winner at this meeting last year when sporting first-time cheekpieces. Gets blinkers for the first time here, with the ground seemingly coming in her favor again. Is 6lb higher than in 2023, but has a decent 5lb claimer in the plate.

Made all to win when hanging on at Navan over 10 furlongs. The drop back one and a half furlongs looks ideal on this tough course. Could make all again as he likes to dominate. 40/1 is a crazy price with only 10 runners.

Enfranchise is rated over 100 on the flat. She won a maiden hurdle race here two years ago but has not added to that win over hurdles. She has mainly run on the flat, winning a Listed race at Gowran in May 2024. This season, she has been placed in two Listed races and one Group 3 race. Danny Mullins rides, and she should be at least placed.

The model I run suggests Radar Ahead can win this one. Radar Ahead lines up here with the highest RPR of the larger 18-runner field but has an official ranking that's closer to the lower middle order. This subsequently leaves Radar Ahead well treated in the weights around his 2m round trip. Won when last out 17 days ago and second on the run before that, so comes here with plenty of form to work with. The model has issued a 'very low stake' indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Decent reappearance run which should put her spot on for this. One of the least exposed here, so hope for more improvement and can go close.
Has been running well. Decent RPRs, can go well on handicap debut in this mares' race. Again, another one with outstanding pedigree.

Fratas has only run 5 times over hurdles but has a win and two runner-up finishes. She won 4 times on the flat in 2023 and was runner-up at Sligo as recently as May. She finished second in her last two starts over hurdles at Bellewstown in April and Ballinrobe in May. She is down 1 lb from those runs with her handicap mark protected for a race like this, and she looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

Mark McNiff's 8 year old Mare RED BALL OF FIRE has me intrigued & at current 33/1 odds there is enough in the profile for me to have a little skin in the game. This Daughter of CANFORD CLIFFS returns off a 276 day sabbatical but if you look back over her form she's never really embarrassed herself when returning off these big breaks but more importantly is this charges record over sharp tracks with ALL of her better form (3 wins 5 places) coming off them aswell a very good record when running in July (with 2 wins 1 place from 4 runs) Now 2lbs lighter than her last win & with Jockey Alan King shedding another 7lbs Im just finding it hard to dismiss her entirely & ill be honest if she was 12's or even 16's id probably pass over her but these odds are too big for me to ias up.

Mont St Michel is rated well ahead of the field in this twelve-furlong maiden. Aidan O'Brien's four-year-old colt has not had that many runs. He was put in with Aidan's Kyprios as a pacemaker in a Group 3 earlier this season and owes his 96 rating for finishing 4th of 5, beaten only three and a quarter lengths in that race. Subsequently, he lost to Royal Hollow in a 14f maiden after trying to make all at a steady pace under his current amateur rider. He should win if overcoming his draw in stall 21 after passing the winning post on the first circuit.

The model I run suggests Word For Word can win this one. Word For Word lines up here with a comparably high RPr of this larger 17-runner field but looks well treated in the weights. Steps out carrying the second lowest amount of weight compared to the other runners and has a weight differential of over 11 lbs to the current market favorite. Drawn in stall 6, which isn't too difficult to overcome over the 1m 4f distance, and the weight differential over this longer distance should be telling. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Arctic Gale is well in on chase form, having won his latest beginners' chase at Tipperary. He also won a bumper back in 2023, and although not winning in eight attempts over hurdles, he finished in 2nd place three times and is overdue a win over hurdles.
Decent run last time out and confirmed he gets the trip well. Really could be anything, and with conditions to suit, can go close.
Related to Kauto Star and really impressed on last run. Eased towards finish. If can step up on that performance, can be right in the mix.

Unexposed 5yo, four starts over hurdles. Getting his act together two weeks ago when winning a 15 runner maiden hurdle, the front two pulling 15L clear of the rest. Trained at a good yard and an opening handicap mark of 110 might underestimate him.
Won from this mark over fences last time out with the second franking the form by winning since and being 20 lbs higher in weights. Has more mileage over hurdles, especially over this trip.

Portarlington justified favouritism to win at Downpatrick with a bold front-running effort. Has another go at this trip, and with ground to suit, looks worth an each-way shout if the last run can be replicated.

Ahead of the Posse has beaten 2 subsequent winners - War Correspondent, who beat odds-on rivals, and Portarlington, who he re-opposes for this contest. Only 2lb higher than last win with claiming jockey retained. Trainer Gavin Cromwell is no stranger to big festival wins. Looks to have scope to improve further.

Caesar Rock has not won since April 22 but looks interesting returned to hurdles following a couple of placed finishes over fences and on the flat this year. He was second, beaten just 4 lengths by Sir Gerhard in a Punchestown flat race in February, and earlier this month was again second in a Novice Chase at Tipperary. This is his first run over hurdles since finishing 4th in a Cork Novice hurdle in May 2022, and off a 4lbs lower mark, it's possible his shrewd trainer has found him a good opportunity. He looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.
Two from two at this course bodes very well, and it must have been trained for another crack back here. So, El Champo looks like a good each-way shot.

Coastal World catches the eye as a runner who has been prepared with this race in mind. After a break of 303 days, he appeared at Cartmel in England. He ran an eye-catching race, running at the rear of the field, coming through to the leaders and then dropping away in the closing stages to finish fourth. The first and third in that race have gone on to win a race each and the second place runner was only beaten by a short head in their subsequent race. If Coastal World can settle, then he could be interesting at a big price.

Looks the type to improve at this trip with hurdles form under her belt. Easily won a 12f maiden here last year, galloping strong to the line, and was eye-catching last time out when staying on into 5th in a decent mares' handicap at Ballinrobe over 1m 5f.

Happy Jacky is now an eleven-year-old but is still at the top of his form, having in the last year won on the flat, over fences, and last time also over hurdles. He has been pushed up in the weights to a mark of 82, giving him top weight here with regular jockey Keithen Kennedy taking off five pounds. He won over further at Down Royal off 74 last September and was a close 3rd of 25 in a similar handicap at the Curragh off 79. Pushed up to a high mark of 72, he should still be competitive.
Has won two bumpers and got off the mark at the third attempt on the flat when winning at Down Royal last time out. In with a real chance on her handicap debut here.
Feud was a creditable fourth last time at Killarney. If improving for that run, he could certainly be involved in the finish here for the Richard John O'Brien yard.

The model I run suggests Pralognan can win this one. Pralognan comes here with a comparably high RPR to the other 19 runners in this larger field, but has an official ranking that leaves him closer to the lower order. Goes out carrying only 3 lbs off the lowest weight but 12 lbs lighter than the top weight. This, coupled with good form coming into this, leaves Pralognan with some opportunity. First when last out 32 days ago and looks to build on that here. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Not ideally placed and given too much to do on reappearance run last time. Should come on for that run and comes here from the same mark. Decent each-way chance for 5 places.
Rated 2lb higher than last year when a beaten favourite, finishing 2nd in this race, could easily go one better here with Heffernan in the saddle.

Dual-purpose mare who has secured 3 flat victories. She placed 5th in a handicap at Killarney 15 days ago, maintaining her pace despite a less than ideal position. The 6-year-old sits 2lb below her last winning mark, and the jockeys 7lb claim adds its appeal. The 20/1 odds offer good value for an each-way bet.

Been running well recently and has looked a shade unlucky not to finish closer than he did in two of his last three starts, both at the Curragh, running on well on both occasions after having to wait for an opening. Posted another solid effort at Fairyhouse last time when 2nd and back in a handicap can go close.

Karl Thornton knows what it takes to win at the Galway Festival, and I think his Rich Belief has an each way chance here, the six-year-old is down to his last winning mark of 75. He looked like he needed the run on his seasonal debut at Down Royal over an inadequate mile and two furlongs two weeks ago. He also has Galway festival form, having run well on his only start here in 2022 when staying on well to finish fourth over a mile and six furlongs.

Absolutely the class angle in this race. Campaigned very cleverly since its emphatic Cheltenham festival win, now it's snuck in at a brilliant weight. Walsh on board same as chelt. Think this is a good bet.

The Galway Hurdle is always very competitive and Joseph O'Brien has obviously been playing around with the well backed favourite, but at a decent price Dysart Enos could go well. He has failed to fully deliver what he promised in his early days, but a fast run race in a big field should suit and if he recaptured his Greatwood hurdle form from Cheltenham in November, he should go very well.

Given Willie Mullins' record in this, 5 out of the last 10 runnings, and the fact Paul Townend has chosen the 6yo mare from a possible 6 runners for the stable, this is too big a price. She's only had 3 runs for the yard, so is unexposed, and this drop back to a stiff 2 miles should suit her, following her good 4th in a competitive handicap at Punchestown's Festival over an extended 2m4f.
